disposition_reason: Table 1 prints per-region mean concentrations of Sr, Pb, As, Zn, Ni, MnO and Cr in dried wild cowberry, blueberry and cranberry.

study.design: field survey of wild berries from background (intact forest) areas
study.origin: wild-harvested in Leningrad, Novgorod, Pskov and Vologda regions, North-West Russia, outside protected natural areas at traditional harvesting places
study.method: X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (SPECTROSCAN-Max G) on berries dried at 20 C and ground

unresolved: Table 1 prints '-' for blueberry lead, Novgorod region, without a footnote; not recorded as a non-detect.

Methods list strontium, lead, zinc, copper, vanadium, chromium and iron, titanium and manganese oxides as analytes, but Table 1 also gives arsenic and nickel and omits copper; the XRF basis for arsenic is not described.
Text says maximum permissible concentrations were exceeded for 'arcenic and mercury', but mercury was not measured; abstract and conclusion say lead and arsenic.
Number of samples per species and region not reported; the ± statistic is not defined.
Table 1 bolds values exceeding Russian maximum permissible concentrations; the bold formatting is lost in text extraction, so exceedance flags are not recorded.
Figure 1 and Figure 2 averages are figure-only and not recorded.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Russian Federation / Eurasian Economic Commission maximum permissible concentrations for heavy metals and arsenic in food raw materials (refs 7, 8)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: values not printed in the paper
